args.summary: Deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate, failing health checks. Rolled back all regions to the most recent healthy production release, v2.3.0. Post-rollback the service is healthy again with an error rate of 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1 also failed in staging as v2.3.1-rc, so the release should be investigated before any redeploy.
args.title: checkout-api outage following v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's what I did:

1. **Diagnosed** the failure: v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rolled back** all production regions to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.2.9 was also healthy, but v2.3.0 is more recent).
3. **Verified** the rollback: checkout-api is now healthy in all regions with an error rate of 0.2%.
4. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) documenting the outage, the rollback, and the recovery — it has paged the on-call engineer.

One note for the on-call engineer in the incident summary: v2.3.1 had also failed health checks in staging as v2.3.1-rc, so the release should be investigated before it's redeployed.
